entry.title: Filipino-Inspired SPAM Silog
entry.summary: Cuisine: Filipino-Inspired Prep Time: 5 minutes Cook Time: 15 minutes Servings: 2 Difficulty: Easy Silog is a popular Filipino breakfast…
entry.content:
Cuisine: Filipino-Inspired
Prep Time: 5 minutes
Cook Time: 15 minutes
Servings: 2
Difficulty: Easy

Description

Silog is a popular Filipino breakfast featuring rice, a fried egg, and a savory main ingredient. This version uses crispy SPAM for a simple, satisfying meal that works any time of day!

Ingredients

  • ½ can SPAM, sliced

  • 2 eggs

  • 2 cups cooked white rice (or cooked lentil-and-rice mixture)

  • 2 cloves garlic, minced (optional)

  • 1 tablespoon cooking oil

  • Vinegar or hot sauce, for serving (optional)

Instructions

  1. Prepare the rice. Cook rice according to the package instructions.

  2. Make garlic rice. If garlic is available, heat a little oil in a skillet and sauté the minced garlic until fragrant. Add the cooked rice and stir-fry for 2–3 minutes.

  3. Fry the SPAM. Cut SPAM into slices and cook in a skillet over medium heat until browned on both sides.

  4. Cook the eggs. Fry the eggs to your preferred doneness, making sure they are cooked thoroughly.

  5. Assemble the plate. Serve the rice alongside the SPAM and fried eggs.

  6. Enjoy! Add vinegar or hot sauce for extra flavor if desired.

Cultural Note

The word silog comes from sinangag (garlic fried rice) and itlog (egg). Filipino silog breakfasts have many variations using different meats and proteins. This recipe is a pantry-friendly adaptation!

entry.title: Hawaiian-Inspired SPAM Fried Rice
entry.summary: Cuisine: Hawaiian-Inspired Prep Time: 10 minutes Cook Time: 15 minutes Servings: 3–4 Difficulty: Easy SPAM is a popular ingredient in…
entry.content:
Cuisine: Hawaiian-Inspired
Prep Time: 10 minutes
Cook Time: 15 minutes
Servings: 3–4
Difficulty: Easy

Description

SPAM is a popular ingredient in Hawaiian home cooking, and fried rice is one of the many ways to enjoy it! This pantry-friendly version combines crispy SPAM, vegetables, eggs, and rice for a comforting one-pan meal.

Ingredients

  • ½ can SPAM, diced

  • 2 cups cooked rice (or cooked lentil-and-rice mixture)

  • 2 eggs

  • 1 carrot, finely chopped

  • ½ onion, diced

  • 1 tablespoon cooking oil

  • 1–2 tablespoons soy sauce (optional)

  • Black pepper, to taste

Instructions

  1. Prepare the rice. Cook rice according to the package instructions. If possible, allow it to cool before frying.

  2. Cook the SPAM. Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add diced SPAM and fry for 4–5 minutes until crispy.

  3. Add the vegetables. Stir in the onion and carrot. Cook until softened, approximately 4 minutes.

  4. Scramble the eggs. Move the SPAM and vegetables to one side of the skillet. Crack in the eggs and scramble until cooked.

  5. Add the rice. Stir in the cooked rice and mix everything together.

  6. Season and serve. Add soy sauce and black pepper, if available. Stir-fry for another 2–3 minutes until everything is heated through.

Pantry Tip

The pantry's lentil-and-rice packets can replace plain rice for extra protein and fiber. The flavor and texture will be a little different, but it's still delicious!

entry.title: SPAM Breakfast Burrito
entry.summary: Cuisine: Mexican-American / Hawaiian-Inspired Prep Time: 10 minutes Cook Time: 15 minutes Servings: 2 Difficulty: Easy Looking for a quick…
entry.content:
Cuisine: Mexican-American / Hawaiian-Inspired
Prep Time: 10 minutes
Cook Time: 15 minutes
Servings: 2
Difficulty: Easy

Description

Looking for a quick and filling breakfast? This SPAM Breakfast Burrito combines crispy SPAM, fluffy scrambled eggs, golden potatoes, and sautéed vegetables, all wrapped in a warm tortilla. It's an easy way to turn everyday pantry ingredients into a delicious meal!

Ingredients

  • ½ can SPAM, diced

  • 2 large flour tortillas

  • 2 eggs

  • 1 medium potato, diced

  • ½ onion, chopped

  • 1 jalapeño, chopped (optional)

  • 1 tablespoon cooking oil

  • Black pepper, to taste

  • Hot sauce (optional)

Instructions

  1. Cook the potatoes. Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add diced potatoes and cook for 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender and golden.

  2. Add the vegetables. Stir in chopped onion and jalapeño. Cook for 3–4 minutes until softened.

  3. Crisp the SPAM. Add diced SPAM and cook until lightly browned, about 4–5 minutes.

  4. Scramble the eggs. Push the other ingredients to one side of the pan. Add the beaten eggs and gently scramble until fully cooked.

  5. Assemble the burritos. Warm the tortillas, divide the filling evenly between them, and wrap tightly.

  6. Serve and enjoy! Add hot sauce or your favorite toppings if available.

Pantry Tip

SPAM is already salty, so you probably won't need extra salt. For an even more filling burrito, add canned chickpeas or lentils.

entry.title: Coconut Tofu Noodle Soup
entry.summary: Serves 2 · About 20 minutes Coconut milk makes a regular packet of instant noodles feel like a whole different…
entry.content:
Serves 2 · About 20 minutes

Coconut milk makes a regular packet of instant noodles feel like a whole different meal.

Ingredients

  • 2 packets instant noodles
  • ½ package tofu, drained and cubed
  • 1 cup canned coconut milk, stirred before measuring
  • 2 cups water
  • ½ onion, thinly sliced
  • 1 teaspoon oil
  • Instant noodle seasoning, to taste
  • Optional: curry powder, chili sauce, or a squeeze of lime

Directions

  1. Heat the oil in a saucepan. Cook the onion over medium heat for about 5 minutes.
  2. If using curry powder, stir in 1 teaspoon and cook for 30 seconds.
  3. Add the coconut milk, water, and tofu. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5 minutes.
  4. Add the noodles and cook according to their package directions.
  5. Stir in a little noodle seasoning at a time, tasting before adding more. Finish with any optional toppings.

entry.title: Tomato & White Bean Pasta

entry.content:
Serves 3–4 · About 25 minutes

A simple pantry version of pasta e fagioli: pasta and beans cooked in a thick tomato broth.

Ingredients

  • 1 can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
  • 1½ cups dry mini penne
  • ½ onion, diced
  • 3 tablespoons tomato paste
  • 1 tablespoon oil
  • 4 cups water
  • Salt and pepper
  • Optional: garlic, Italian seasoning, or chili flakes

Directions

  1. Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
  2. Stir in the tomato paste and any optional seasonings. Cook for 1 minute.
  3. Add the water and beans. Bring to a boil, then stir in the pasta.
  4. Simmer, stirring frequently, until the pasta is tender, about 10–15 minutes. Add more water if it gets too thick.
  5. Mash a few beans against the side of the pot to thicken the broth. Season to taste.
